chapter: Reel 2-3: tunes, closing and country life
title: Card games and a whist story
summary: Allen asks about card games; Mrs. Clementin tells of playing whist and a game she won on a boat trip.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: What card games did you play? What kind of card games? You played vocal? I played guitar. Play guitar? Yeah. I'm not that.
But you don't like to play? I didn't play much card. I didn't play whist. Play whist.
Whist is not so popular in other towns. Well whist is like...
Yeah, it's like bridge, they tell me.

Yeah, whist would be a good game. Nice game. I had to take a few hours for pleasure. But whist? Oh yes, you have to be good people to keep you whist. Yeah. We went across the lake one time. We had some friends. And my mom, my mom, my mom, my mom, my mom. And we had some old friends. We had to go across the lake. We had to go on the boat. We had to go to Oakland When we got over there right away, so they told me we're going to meet you now. Nobody could meet me. That last game, I had to let it be so I couldn't stop. Everybody picked the boat on the boat and that means I couldn't stop. If they want me to stop, they want me to stay over there then, you see? They didn't have to pick the boat. I was half-dressed around to come in case my mother took my cow and was about five years old. She was like, come on, come on, you don't need to go. My father, I just didn't meet him and got on that boat. And that's funny. And all the time, when we had a big game, my broad-law here, who used to work, just for saying, I was not that busy. When he felt that he was going to meet me, he was busy. Sometimes, I used to push on the center, but sometimes I used to love him, but he never cared. He used to. So he turned around, he was playing. I let him play all his big hands. And I had that rope. And I had that rope. He would think that I fixed it. I was done the one game. But you would think that the hand was fixed from the ears down to the loose. And I let him play his, you know, few hands he had. Then when he gave me, he put that rope down, that was all. That was all. He made a mistake. When he put that in, he had that key in his hand and he got released from the hand. So many other things he had, you understand? But when I took the rope, all his hand was dead. His family was dead. My father, he didn't have rope. All the rope was in my hand. And then the left, he stood there. Uncle, he said, mother's dead. Then he left, he said, man, you've been a good boy. You've been trusted, but why should he? He said, I've never been back no more. He never bring me no more either. Just because I did. Because there was a lot of time, he said, well, you were such a wonderful boy. And so you can make a mistake sometimes. I used to love it, but after that, when I started to bring my body, one thing with me. I loved it. Then I started to bring that down. But pay it back, I never really get much pay it back. Use your money to pay it. I like some working pay, but at the end of the pay, but I got the hand on the pay, but I got it now. I got it back.
